statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases from 17 to 14 because the recovery the previous assessment could only call intact has since extended. NQ futures were verified at 29,233.75, down 215.00 points or 0.73% from a 29,448.75 close, roughly 190 points above a 29,044.25 session low that has now held for more than two cash hours without being retested. Cash NAS100 at 29,205.87 independently confirms the shape: its session high has been extended to 29,250.41 from 29,177.14 an hour ago, so the index is making progressively higher highs after opening the auction at its session low of 29,038.22. VIX at 17.24, up about 4.7%, has decayed from an 18.05 session high, which is the volatility signature of orderly rather than disorderly discovery. The unresolved counterweight is energy: Brent at $105.82 is up 4.55% and WTI at $100.50 is up 4.63%, both at fresh session highs and both higher than an hour ago, while the ten-year Treasury yield at 4.92% and the two-year at 4.53% sit near the day's highs. Crude making new highs while the index recovers is dispersion, not the aligned amplifier stack that a no-retracement path requires.
recommendation: Tail at 14 maps the policy state to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, with pause false and caution false under the fixed repository mapping. The danger window remains drawn narrowly around 12:30 to 13:30 UTC on 11 September, covering the August consumer price index and the first full hour of post-release price discovery, which is the next scheduled point at which a no-retracement structure could plausibly form. Conditional tail reaches 22 in the 12:00 UTC slot tomorrow and 20 in the hour after; those are the only two slots in the forward window mapped to the watch band. A secondary conditional peak of 18 to 19 sits in the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots today, where U.S. cash trading closes and Oracle reports fiscal Q1 2027 results into materially thinner futures liquidity; that peak stays inside the low band because thin-book reactions are normally discontinuous gaps rather than sustained one-way paths, and because Oracle is NYSE-listed, so its transmission to the Nasdaq-100 runs through sentiment in the semiconductor complex rather than through index weight. Stress remains extreme at 84 because the energy-led inflation impulse, an ECB that raised rates today with effect from 16 September and a Federal Reserve decision on 16 September are all unresolved. Stress at that level describes the environment and does not on its own move the mapped state past the blocking threshold.
headline: NQ extends its recovery to about 190 points off the 29,044.25 low and cash NAS100 makes a new session high at 29,250.41, while Brent pushes to $105.82; tail eases from 17 to 14
body:
The reversal identified an hour ago has not merely held, it has extended, and that is the single most important fact for a mean-reversion book.

NQ futures were verified at 29,233.75, down 215.00 points or 0.73%, against a session range of 29,044.25 to 29,508.25. An hour ago the same contract was at 29,161.00, down 0.98%, about 117 points off the low. The low is unchanged, the distance from it has grown by roughly seventy points, and the percentage loss on the day has narrowed. The cash index confirms this independently rather than merely echoing it: the Nasdaq-100 stands at 29,205.87 against a range of 29,038.22 to 29,250.41, and that high is new. An hour ago the session high was 29,177.14. The index has therefore printed a higher high after opening the auction at its session low, which is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, failed-retracement structure that defines a pathological path.

The volatility surface agrees. VIX at 17.24 is up about 4.7% on the day but has decayed from a session high of 18.05, and an hour ago it was at 17.98 and up 9.25%. Implied volatility falling while the index recovers is the signature of price discovery working, not of a market repricing in one direction without pause.

The evidence pulling the other way is energy, and it is not weakening. Brent at $105.82 is up 4.55% and WTI at $100.50 is up 4.63%, both at their highest since 19 May, and both higher than the 104.05 and 2.80% observed an hour ago. Trading Economics attributes the move to escalating Middle East tensions and reduced Saudi production. The ten-year Treasury yield at 4.92% is up about 7.8 basis points and the two-year at 4.53% is up about 8.7, both near session highs, and the thirty-year sits at 5.35%. The transmission channel is explicit in today's data: the August producer price index published at 12:30 UTC showed final demand up 0.4% on the month with over three quarters of the goods rise attributable to energy, which rose 4.2%, and diesel up 24.1%. Final demand less foods, energy and trade services rose 0.3%, and the twelve-month rate stands at 5.4%.

For tail scoring the relevant question is whether these inputs are aligned. They are not. Crude is making new session highs at the same time as the index is making higher intraday highs, and the sector picture is similarly split, with the semiconductor cohort broadly lower while several megacaps trade higher on the latest session's data. That is dispersion. A pathological no-retracement path normally requires the opposite: cross-assets moving together, retracements failing, and the index holding at its extreme. None of those three conditions is present at 15:00 UTC, so tail moves to 14 and the dominant mode is read as mixed.

Stress stays at 84 and in the extreme band, which is the honest description of an environment where an energy shock is feeding a producer-price impulse, the ECB raised all three key rates by 25 basis points today with effect from 16 September, and the Federal Reserve decides on 16 September with the market having begun to price renewed tightening. High stress coexisting with low tail is the expected configuration on a day where a large adverse move occurred and was then absorbed in an orderly way.

Two forward checkpoints are worth naming and neither is treated as observed. The U.S. cash close at 20:00 UTC is followed by Oracle's fiscal Q1 2027 results and a 21:00 UTC call, into futures liquidity that thins sharply after the close; conditional tail is lifted to 18 and 19 across those two slots. The August consumer price index at 12:30 UTC on 11 September is the larger of the two, and conditional tail reaches 22 in the slot containing it and 20 in the hour after, the only two watch-band slots in the forward window. Today's producer-price release is the closest available analogue and it produced a low that held and a recovery, which is why the post-release slots are scored to decay rather than to extend.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 15:00 UTC on 9 September to 14:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 16 with an event/whipsaw read, settles quickly into a 13 to 8 band across the U.S. close and the overnight session, and holds a narrow 9 to 11 range with a mixed dominant mode through the Asian and early European hours. The turn sits in the final four slots: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode switched to trend-down on the pre-release grind, tail 20 at 12:00 UTC with the mapped state at WATCH around the producer price release, tail 24 at 13:00 UTC read as trend-down after the release extended the session low, and tail 17 at 14:00 UTC once the opening auction reversed rather than continued. Stress never left the extreme band across the whole window, ranging from 80 to 86, which is the clearest single feature of the period: a difficult high-volatility environment coexisted with a tail score that stayed below the blocking threshold for all 24 hours. Past assessments are reported exactly as published and are not revised with later information.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with the intraday recovery confirmed and extended, and closes on a consumer price release. Conditional tail starts at 14 in the current 15:00 UTC hour, eases to 13 through the early afternoon, ticks to 14 around the WTI settlement and reaches 16 in the 19:00 UTC power hour. It then rises to 18 and 19 across the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots, which contain the U.S. cash close and Oracle's fiscal Q1 2027 results into thin futures liquidity, before decaying through 16 and 13 into the late evening. Overnight the path settles to a 10 to 11 floor across the Asian session, then climbs gradually through 11, 12, 12, 13, 14 and 15 as European trade and pre-release positioning build, reaching 22 in the 12:00 UTC slot that contains the August consumer price index and 20 in the hour after it, before easing to 17 around the University of Michigan survey at 14:00 UTC. Those two release slots are the only ones mapped to the watch band, and the danger window is drawn narrowly around 12:30 to 13:30 UTC on 11 September. The anticipatory climb raises stress and lowers confidence faster than it raises tail, because hypothetical post-event alignment is not scored as though it had already been observed. Stress runs from 84 down to a 78 overnight trough and back to a 87 peak in the release slot, while confidence holds between 80 and 88.
